speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is causing this, can you tell me if you are vomiting, and if so, does it look like bile (green) or if there is blood in it?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds painful; does your baby have episodes of drawing their knees up to their chest, followed by passing small, hard, or ribbon-like stools? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The clinical presentation of colicky pain (drawing knees up), irritability, and the X-ray findings of a dilated bowel with no gas in the rectum are highly suggestive of an intestinal obstruction caused by intussusception.
